    16	#ifndef XLA_PJRT_PLUGIN_XLA_GPU_XLA_GPU_ALLOCATOR_CONFIG_H_
    17	#define XLA_PJRT_PLUGIN_XLA_GPU_XLA_GPU_ALLOCATOR_CONFIG_H_
    18	
    19	#include <cstddef>
    20	#include <cstdint>
    21	#include <optional>
    22	#include <vector>
    23	
    24	#include "xla/tsl/framework/allocator.h"
    25	
    26	namespace xla {
    27	
    28	struct GpuAllocatorConfig {
    29	  enum class Kind {
    30	    kDefault,   // Client picks the best option for the platform.
    31	    kPlatform,  // Synchronous passthrough allocator that calls the
    32	                // StreamExecutor Allocate/Deallocate APIs directly via a
    33	                // MultiDeviceAdapter wrapping StreamExecutorAllocator
    34	                // instances, with no BFC caching or pooled growth.
    35	    kBFC,  // Allocator using a "Best-Fit with Coalescing" algorithm. Currently
    36	           // only available for GPU.
    37	    kCudaAsync,  // Use the CUDA async allocator.
    38	    kVmm,  // Use Virtual Memory Management (VMM) allocator. This allocator
    39	           // uses CUDA VMM APIs to manage virtual address space separately from
    40	           // physical memory, enabling features like memory oversubscription
    41	           // and fine-grained memory mapping control.
    42	  };
    43	  Kind kind = Kind::kDefault;
    44	
    45	  // Only used if kind == kBFC. The maximum fraction of available memory to
    46	  // allocate. This is the default value of XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION.
    47	  //
    48	  // If `gpu_system_memory_size` is set, it determines memory allocation.
    49	  // `memory_fraction` won't be used in this case.
    50	  double memory_fraction = 0.75;
    51	
    52	  // Only used if kind == kBFC. The absolute size of reserved memory space for
    53	  // GPU system in bytes.
    54	  //
    55	  // If null, the default value `memory_fraction` will be used.
    56	  std::optional<int64_t> gpu_system_memory_size = std::nullopt;
    57	
    58	  // Only used if kind == kBFC. If true, the allocator will immediately allocate
    59	  // the maximum amount allowed by `memory_fraction`. This reduces
    60	  // fragmentation, allowing more of the total memory to be used. If false, the
    61	  // allocator will allocate more memory as allocations are requested.
    62	  bool preallocate = true;
    63	
    64	  // Amount of collective memory (ncclMemAlloc) to preallocate. If this value is
    65	  // 0, collective memory space will be grown as needed to fit the application's
    66	  // usage, with the drawback of potentially higher fragmentation. If set,
    67	  // should be set to a multiple of 512MB to avoid wasting memory due to
    68	  // granularity requirements.
    69	  size_t collective_memory_size = 0;
    70	
    71	  // Callbacks that get called when the underlying suballocator allocates or
    72	  // deallocates memory. See `SubAllocator::Visitor` for more details.
    73	  std::vector<tsl::SubAllocator::Visitor> sub_allocator_alloc_visitors;
    74	  std::vector<tsl::SubAllocator::Visitor> sub_allocator_free_visitors;
    75	};
    76

    44	struct GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::CudaState {
    45	  // cudaMallocAsync is stream aware. But TF StreamExecutor use only 1
    46	  // compute stream and already synchronize with the h2d, d2h and d2d
    47	  // stream. So we do not need to ask cudaMallocAsync to add extra
    48	  // synchronization.
    49	  // Not owned.
    50	  CUstream cuda_stream{};
    51	
    52	  // Not owned. The default pool of the associated GPU.
    53	  // If null, then the instantiation failed and the first allocation
    54	  // will return an error.
    55	  CUmemoryPool pool{};
    56	};

    58	void GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::PrintAllocatorStatisticsNoLock() {
    59	  std::map<size_t, int> size_map_histogram;
    60	  std::vector<std::string> ptr_size_string;
    61	  for (auto p : size_map_) {
    62	    if (VLOG_IS_ON(8)) {
    63	      ptr_size_string.push_back(
    64	          absl::StrCat("(", absl::Hex(p.first), ",", p.second) + ")");
    65	    }
    66	    size_map_histogram[p.second]++;
    67	  }
    68	  LOG(ERROR) << "Histogram of current allocation: (allocation_size_in_bytes, "
    69	             << "nb_allocation_of_that_sizes), ...;";
    70	  for (auto p : size_map_histogram) {
    71	    LOG(ERROR) << p.first << ", " << p.second;
    72	  }
    73	
    74	  VLOG(8) << "\nThe sorted list of (ptr,size):";
    75	  VLOG(8) << absl::StrJoin(ptr_size_string, ",");
    76	
    77	  cuuint64_t mem_reserved_current;
    78	  if (auto result = cuMemPoolGetAttribute(cuda_state_->pool,
    79	                                          CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_RESERVED_MEM_CURRENT,
    80	                                          &mem_reserved_current)) {
    81	    LOG(ERROR) << "Error while fetching extra cudaMallocAsync pool attribute: "
    82	               << cuda::ToStatus(result);
    83	  }
    84	  cuuint64_t mem_used_current;
    85	  if (auto result = cuMemPoolGetAttribute(cuda_state_->pool,
    86	                                          CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_USED_MEM_CURRENT,
    87	                                          &mem_used_current)) {
    88	    LOG(ERROR) << "Error while fetching extra cudaMallocAsync pool attribute: "
    89	               << cuda::ToStatus(result);
    90	  }
    91	  cuuint64_t mem_reserved_high;
    92	  if (auto result = cuMemPoolGetAttribute(cuda_state_->pool,
    93	                                          CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_RESERVED_MEM_HIGH,
    94	                                          &mem_reserved_high)) {
    95	    LOG(ERROR) << "Error while fetching extra cudaMallocAsync pool attribute: "
    96	               << cuda::ToStatus(result);
    97	  }
    98	  cuuint64_t mem_used_high;
    99	  if (auto result = cuMemPoolGetAttribute(
   100	          cuda_state_->pool, CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_USED_MEM_HIGH, &mem_used_high)) {
   101	    LOG(ERROR) << "Error while fetching extra cudaMallocAsync pool attribute: "
   102	               << cuda::ToStatus(result);
   103	  }
   104	  LOG(ERROR) << "CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_RESERVED_MEM_CURRENT: "
   105	             << mem_reserved_current;
   106	  LOG(ERROR) << "CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_USED_MEM_CURRENT: " << mem_used_current;
   107	  LOG(ERROR) << "CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_RESERVED_MEM_HIGH: " << mem_reserved_high;
   108	  LOG(ERROR) << "CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_USED_MEM_HIGH: " << mem_used_high;
   109	}

   111	std::atomic<int> GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::number_instantiated_(0);
   112	
   113	GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator(
   114	    tsl::PlatformDeviceId platform_device_id, bool create_new_pool,
   115	    size_t new_pool_size, bool reserve_memory, size_t reserve_memory_size,
   116	    bool sync_mode, bool compute_stats)
   117	    : cuda_state_{std::make_unique<CudaState>()},
   118	      name_(absl::StrCat("gpu_async_", platform_device_id.value())),
   119	      reserve_memory_(reserve_memory),
   120	      create_new_pool_(create_new_pool),
   121	      sync_mode_(sync_mode) {
   122	  ++number_instantiated_;
   123	
   124	  stream_exec_ = GPUMachineManager()
   125	                     ->ExecutorForDevice(platform_device_id.value())
   126	                     .value();
   127	
   128	  int driverVersion;
   129	  cuDriverGetVersion(&driverVersion);
   130	  VLOG(2) << "DRIVER VERSION: " << driverVersion;
   131	  if (driverVersion < 11020) {
   132	    LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   133	        << "Disable cuda_malloc_async or update your CUDA driver to a version"
   134	        << " compatible with CUDA 11.2 or higher."
   135	        << " We detected a version compatible with: " << driverVersion;
   136	  }
   137	
   138	  // WAR an CUDA 11.2 driver bug for multiple-GPU. It currently
   139	  // request that the context on GPU 0 is initialized. Which isn't the
   140	  // case for TF+horovod.
   141	  if (platform_device_id.value() > 0 && driverVersion < 11030) {
   142	    CUcontext pctx;  // We loose track of it. But this is fine.
   143	    if (auto result = cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain(&pctx, 0))
   144	      LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   145	          << "Failed to retain context: " << cuda::ToStatus(result);
   146	  }
   147	
   148	  std::unique_ptr<ActivateContext> scoped_activation = stream_exec_->Activate();
   149	
   150	  // Check the CUDA runtime is recent enough.
   151	  if (auto status2 = cuDriverGetVersion(&driverVersion)) {
   152	    LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   153	        << "Error while fetching driver version: " << cuda::ToStatus(status2);
   154	  }
   155	
   156	  // Check that cudaMallocAsync is supported.
   157	  int cuda_malloc_async_supported;
   158	  if (auto status =
   159	          cuDeviceGetAttribute(&cuda_malloc_async_supported,
   160	                               CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MEMORY_POOLS_SUPPORTED,
   161	                               platform_device_id.value())) {
   162	    LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   163	        << "On device: " << platform_device_id.value()
   164	        << " Current driver: " << driverVersion
   165	        << ". Failed to get device attribute : " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   166	  }
   167	  if (!cuda_malloc_async_supported)
   168	    LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   169	        << "TF_GPU_ALLOCATOR=cuda_malloc_async isn't currently supported on "
   170	        << "GPU id " << platform_device_id.value() << ":"
   171	        << " Possible causes: device not supported (request SM60+), driver too "
   172	           "old, "
   173	        << " OS not supported, CUDA version too old(request CUDA11.2+).";
   174	
   175	  size_t pool_size;
   176	  if (create_new_pool_) {
   177	    pool_size = new_pool_size;
   178	    CUmemPoolProps pool_props;
   179	    memset(reinterpret_cast<void*>(&pool_props), 0, sizeof(pool_props));
   180	    pool_props.allocType = CU_MEM_ALLOCATION_TYPE_PINNED;
   181	    pool_props.handleTypes = CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_NONE;
   182	    pool_props.location.id = platform_device_id.value();
   183	    pool_props.location.type = CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE;
   184	#if CUDA_VERSION >= 12030
   185	    pool_props.maxSize = new_pool_size;
   186	#endif  // CUDA_VERSION >= 12030
   187	    if (auto status = cuMemPoolCreate(&cuda_state_->pool, &pool_props))
   188	      LOG(FATAL) <<  // Crash OK.
   189	          "Failed to create CUDA pool: " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   190	  } else {
   191	    pool_size = reserve_memory_size;
   192	    if (auto status = cuDeviceGetDefaultMemPool(&cuda_state_->pool,
   193	                                                platform_device_id.value()))
   194	      LOG(FATAL) <<  // Crash OK.
   195	          "Failed to get default CUDA pool: " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   196	    VLOG(2) << "using default memory pool " << cuda_state_->pool;
   197	  }
   198	
   199	  VLOG(1) << Name() << " CudaMallocAsync initialized on platform: "
   200	          << platform_device_id.value() << " with pool size of: " << pool_size
   201	          << " this ptr: " << this;
   202	  uint64_t release_threshold_64 = reserve_memory_size;
   203	  if (auto status = cuMemPoolSetAttribute(cuda_state_->pool,
   204	                                          CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_RELEASE_THRESHOLD,
   205	                                          &release_threshold_64))
   206	    LOG(FATAL) <<  // Crash OK.
   207	        "Failed to set CUDA pool attribute: " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   208	
   209	  if (compute_stats) {
   210	    stats_ = std::make_unique<tsl::AllocatorStats>();
   211	    stats_->bytes_limit = static_cast<int64_t>(pool_size);
   212	  }  // If not set, it means we do not compute stats.
   213	
   214	  // If in TF_DETERMINISTIC_ALLOCATOR is set, then make the allocator behave
   215	  // determistically.
   216	  bool deterministic = false;
   217	  CHECK_OK(tsl::ReadBoolFromEnvVar("TF_DETERMINISTIC_ALLOCATOR",
   218	                                   /*default_val=*/false, &deterministic));
   219	  if (deterministic) {
   220	    int disable = 0;
   221	    if (auto status = cuMemPoolSetAttribute(
   222	            cuda_state_->pool, CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_REUSE_ALLOW_OPPORTUNISTIC,
   223	            &disable)) {
   224	      LOG(FATAL) <<  // Crash OK.
   225	          "Failed to set CUDA pool attribute: " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   226	    }
   227	    if (auto status = cuMemPoolSetAttribute(
   228	            cuda_state_->pool,
   229	            CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_REUSE_ALLOW_INTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES, &disable)) {
   230	      LOG(FATAL) <<  // Crash OK.
   231	          "Failed to set CUDA pool attribute: " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   232	    }
   233	  }
   234	
   235	  // Set read/write access to all GPUs.
   236	  static auto* const all_pools_ = new std::vector<CUmemoryPool>();
   237	  static auto* const all_ids_ = new std::vector<tsl::PlatformDeviceId>();
   238	  DCHECK(all_pools_->size() == all_ids_->size());
   239	
   240	  // If the cuda_state_->pool is found in all_pools_, it means it has been
   241	  // initialized before. This can happen in some cases, such as when multiple
   242	  // virtual devices are created from one physical GPU, the virtual devices
   243	  // will actually share the same CUDA memory pool. So the following pool
   244	  // initialization steps should be skipped to avoid duplicated initialization
   245	  // of the same pool.
   246	  for (auto pool_item_ : *all_pools_) {
   247	    if (pool_item_ == cuda_state_->pool) {
   248	      VLOG(2) << Name()
   249	              << " GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator pool already initialized. "
   250	                 "PoolSize "
   251	              << pool_size;
   252	      return;
   253	    }
   254	  }
   255	  for (int i = 0; i < all_pools_->size(); ++i) {
   256	    // Set the current pool access to the previous GPUs.
   257	    CUmemAccessDesc map;
   258	    map.flags = CU_MEM_ACCESS_FLAGS_PROT_READWRITE;
   259	    map.location.id = (*all_ids_)[i].value();
   260	
   261	    map.location.type = CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE;
   262	    VLOG(2) << "Setting access of the current pool to "
   263	            << " location id: " << map.location.id;
   264	    int canAccessPeer;
   265	    if (auto status = cuDeviceCanAccessPeer(
   266	            &canAccessPeer, platform_device_id.value(), map.location.id)) {
   267	      cuda_state_->pool = nullptr;
   268	      LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   269	          << "cuDeviceCanAccessPeer failed to know if GPU id "
   270	          << map.location.id << " can access GPU id "
   271	          << platform_device_id.value() << ": " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   272	    }
   273	    if (canAccessPeer == 1) {
   274	      if (auto status = cuMemPoolSetAccess(cuda_state_->pool, &map, 1)) {
   275	        cuda_state_->pool = nullptr;
   276	        LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   277	            << "Error when setting access to the pool id: " << i
   278	            << " location id: " << map.location.id
   279	            << " error: " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   280	      }
   281	    }
   282	
   283	    // Set the previous pools access to the current GPU.
   284	    map.location.id = platform_device_id.value();
   285	
   286	    int previous_pool_id = (*all_ids_)[i].value();
   287	    VLOG(2) << "Set access to the pool id: " << previous_pool_id
   288	            << " location id: " << map.location.id;
   289	    if (auto status = cuDeviceCanAccessPeer(&canAccessPeer, previous_pool_id,
   290	                                            platform_device_id.value())) {
   291	      cuda_state_->pool = nullptr;
   292	      LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   293	          << "cuDeviceCanAccessPeer failed: " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   294	    }
   295	    if (canAccessPeer == 1) {
   296	      if (auto status = cuMemPoolSetAccess((*all_pools_)[i], &map, 1)) {
   297	        cuda_state_->pool = nullptr;
   298	        LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   299	            << "Error when setting access to the pool id: " << previous_pool_id
   300	            << " location id: " << map.location.id
   301	            << " error: " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   302	      }
   303	    }
   304	  }
   305	  all_pools_->push_back(cuda_state_->pool);
   306	  all_ids_->push_back(platform_device_id);
   307	
   308	  VLOG(2) << Name() << " GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator PoolSize " << pool_size;
   309	}
   310	
   311	GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator(
   312	    tsl::PlatformDeviceId platform_device_id, size_t release_threshold,
   313	    bool reserve_memory, bool compute_stats)
   314	    : GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator(platform_device_id, false, 0, reserve_memory,
   315	                                  release_threshold, false, compute_stats) {}
   316	
   317	GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::~GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator() {
   318	  if (create_new_pool_) {
   319	    VLOG(2) << "Delete memory pool "
   320	            << reinterpret_cast<void*>(cuda_state_->pool);
   321	    if (auto status = cuMemPoolDestroy(cuda_state_->pool))
   322	      LOG(FATAL) << "Failed to destroy memory pool:" << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   323	  }
   324	}

   326	void* GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::AllocateRaw(size_t alignment,
   327	                                               size_t num_bytes) {
   328	  CHECK(cuda_state_->cuda_stream != nullptr)
   329	      << "A stream must be added to the GpuCudaMallocAsync allocator";
   330	  if (cuda_state_->pool == nullptr) {
   331	    LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   332	        << "The instantiation of GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator failed."
   333	        << " See previous errors.";
   334	  }
   335	  // The lock is only needed when stats are enabled, but it must be around
   336	  // the cuMemAllocFromPoolAsync call as well to ensure consistency of the stats
   337	  // update.
   338	  std::optional<absl::MutexLock> lock;
   339	  if (stats_) {
   340	    lock.emplace(&mutex_);
   341	  }
   342	  std::unique_ptr<ActivateContext> scoped_activation = stream_exec_->Activate();
   343	  void* ptr = nullptr;
   344	  auto result =
   345	      cuMemAllocFromPoolAsync(reinterpret_cast<CUdeviceptr*>(&ptr), num_bytes,
   346	                              cuda_state_->pool, cuda_state_->cuda_stream);
   347	  if (result == CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY) {
   348	    // Doing a stream synchronization give the driver more flexibility
   349	    // for blocks coalescing and doing memory remapping. So it can
   350	    // solve some OOM cases when memory is tight.
   351	    cuStreamSynchronize(cuda_state_->cuda_stream);
   352	    result =
   353	        cuMemAllocFromPoolAsync(reinterpret_cast<CUdeviceptr*>(&ptr), num_bytes,
   354	                                cuda_state_->pool, cuda_state_->cuda_stream);
   355	  }
   356	  if (result) {
   357	    size_t free, total;
   358	    cuMemGetInfo(&free, &total);
   359	    LOG(ERROR) << Name() << " cuMemAllocAsync failed to allocate " << num_bytes
   360	               << " bytes: " << cuda::ToStatus(result)

   326	void* GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::AllocateRaw(size_t alignment,
   327	                                               size_t num_bytes) {
   328	  CHECK(cuda_state_->cuda_stream != nullptr)
   329	      << "A stream must be added to the GpuCudaMallocAsync allocator";
   330	  if (cuda_state_->pool == nullptr) {
   331	    LOG(FATAL)  // Crash OK.
   332	        << "The instantiation of GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator failed."
   333	        << " See previous errors.";
   334	  }
   335	  // The lock is only needed when stats are enabled, but it must be around
   336	  // the cuMemAllocFromPoolAsync call as well to ensure consistency of the stats
   337	  // update.
   338	  std::optional<absl::MutexLock> lock;
   339	  if (stats_) {
   340	    lock.emplace(&mutex_);
   341	  }
   342	  std::unique_ptr<ActivateContext> scoped_activation = stream_exec_->Activate();
   343	  void* ptr = nullptr;
   344	  auto result =
   345	      cuMemAllocFromPoolAsync(reinterpret_cast<CUdeviceptr*>(&ptr), num_bytes,
   346	                              cuda_state_->pool, cuda_state_->cuda_stream);
   347	  if (result == CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY) {
   348	    // Doing a stream synchronization give the driver more flexibility
   349	    // for blocks coalescing and doing memory remapping. So it can
   350	    // solve some OOM cases when memory is tight.
   351	    cuStreamSynchronize(cuda_state_->cuda_stream);
   352	    result =
   353	        cuMemAllocFromPoolAsync(reinterpret_cast<CUdeviceptr*>(&ptr), num_bytes,
   354	                                cuda_state_->pool, cuda_state_->cuda_stream);
   355	  }
   356	  if (result) {
   357	    size_t free, total;
   358	    cuMemGetInfo(&free, &total);
   359	    LOG(ERROR) << Name() << " cuMemAllocAsync failed to allocate " << num_bytes
   360	               << " bytes: " << cuda::ToStatus(result)
   361	               << "\n Reported by CUDA: Free memory/Total memory: " << free
   362	               << "/" << total;
   363	    if (stats_) {
   364	      LOG(ERROR) << "Stats: " << stats_->DebugString();
   365	      PrintAllocatorStatisticsNoLock();
   366	    }
   367	
   368	    return nullptr;
   369	  }
   370	
   371	  if (sync_mode_) {
   372	    cuStreamSynchronize(cuda_state_->cuda_stream);
   373	  }
   374	
   375	  // Update stats.
   376	  if (stats_) {
   377	    ++(stats_->num_allocs);
   378	    stats_->bytes_in_use += num_bytes;
   379	    if (stats_->bytes_in_use > stats_->peak_bytes_in_use) {
   380	      VLOG(9) << "New Peak memory usage of " << stats_->bytes_in_use
   381	              << " bytes.";
   382	    }
   383	    stats_->peak_bytes_in_use =
   384	        std::max(stats_->peak_bytes_in_use, stats_->bytes_in_use);
   385	    stats_->largest_alloc_size =
   386	        std::max<std::size_t>(stats_->largest_alloc_size, num_bytes);
   387	    bool ptr_inserted = size_map_.emplace(ptr, num_bytes).second;
   388	    DCHECK(ptr_inserted);
   389	  }
   390	  VLOG(10) << Name() << " Allocated " << num_bytes << " at " << ptr;
   391	  return ptr;
   392	}
   393	
   394	void GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::DeallocateRaw(void* ptr) {
   395	  if (ptr == nullptr) return;
   396	  // The lock is only needed when stats are enabled, but it must be around
   397	  // the cuMemFreeAsync call as well to ensure consistency of the stats update.
   398	  std::optional<absl::MutexLock> lock;
   399	  if (stats_) {
   400	    lock.emplace(&mutex_);
   401	  }
   402	  if (auto result = cuMemFreeAsync(reinterpret_cast<const CUdeviceptr&>(ptr),
   403	                                   cuda_state_->cuda_stream)) {
   404	    if (result == CUDA_ERROR_DEINITIALIZED) {
   405	      // It happens with multi-GPU that TF free the GPU allocation after
   406	      // the driver is unloaded. It is safe to ignore this error here.
   407	      // TODO: Find how to fix the shutdown steps in TF.
   408	      VLOG(1) << "Ignoring CUDA error: " << cuda::ToStatus(result);
   409	    } else {
   410	      size_t free, total;
   411	      std::unique_ptr<ActivateContext> scoped_activation =
   412	          stream_exec_->Activate();
   413	      cuMemGetInfo(&free, &total);
   414	      LOG(ERROR) << "cudaFreeAsync failed to free " << ptr << ": "
   415	                 << cuda::ToStatus(result)
   416	                 << "\n Free memory/Total memory: " << free << "/" << total;
   417	      if (stats_) {
   418	        LOG(ERROR) << "Stats: " << stats_->DebugString();
   419	      }
   420	    }
   421	  }
   422	
   423	  if (sync_mode_) {
   424	    cuStreamSynchronize(cuda_state_->cuda_stream);
   425	  }
   426	
   427	  // Updates the stats.
   428	  if (stats_) {
   429	    DCHECK(size_map_.contains(ptr));
   430	    size_t size = size_map_[ptr];
   431	    stats_->bytes_in_use -= size;
   432	    size_map_.erase(ptr);
   433	  }
   434	
   435	  VLOG(10) << Name() << " Freed ptr: " << ptr;
   436	}
   437	
   438	bool GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::TracksAllocationSizes() const {
   439	  return static_cast<bool>(stats_);
   440	}
   441	
   442	size_t GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::RequestedSize(const void* ptr) const {
   443	  if (!stats_ || !ptr) return 0;
   444	  absl::MutexLock l(mutex_);

   469	void GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::SetStreamAndPreallocateMemory(void* stream) {
   470	  auto new_cuda_stream = static_cast<CUstream>(stream);
   471	  // We don't need to re-set the CUDA stream if this is the same stream
   472	  if (cuda_state_->cuda_stream != nullptr &&
   473	      new_cuda_stream != cuda_state_->cuda_stream) {
   474	    LOG(FATAL) <<  // Crash OK.
   475	        "Trying to set the stream twice. This isn't supported. ";
   476	  }
   477	
   478	  uint64_t pool_size_64 = 0;
   479	  if (auto status = cuMemPoolGetAttribute(cuda_state_->pool,
   480	                                          CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_RELEASE_THRESHOLD,
   481	                                          &pool_size_64)) {
   482	    LOG(FATAL) <<  // Crash OK.
   483	        "Failed to get CUDA pool attribute: " << cuda::ToStatus(status);
   484	  }
   485	  cuda_state_->cuda_stream = new_cuda_stream;
   486	  int64_t prealloc_size = 0;
   487	  // TF_CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC_SUPPORTED_PREALLOC=-1 is a special value that
   488	  // preallocates the total pool size.
   489	  CHECK_OK(tsl::ReadInt64FromEnvVar("TF_CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC_SUPPORTED_PREALLOC",
   490	                                    0, &prealloc_size));
   491	  if (prealloc_size == -1) {
   492	    prealloc_size = pool_size_64;
   493	  } else if (reserve_memory_) {
   494	    prealloc_size = pool_size_64;
   495	  }
   496	
   497	  if (prealloc_size != 0) {
   498	    void* ptr = AllocateRaw(0, prealloc_size);
   499	    DeallocateRaw(ptr);
   500	    VLOG(2) << Name() << " GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator reserved the pool for "
   501	            << prealloc_size << " bytes" << ". First ptr: " << ptr;
   502	    ClearStats();
   503	  }
   504	}

1715-  1715	// In a nested loop structure, this calculates the final value of the outer loop
1716-  1716	// induction variable without executing the inner loop. It determines the total
1717-  1717	// number of iterations by computing the ceiling of the distance to the bound
1718-  1718	// i.e.((bound - start + step - 1) / step). It guards against negative
1719-  1719	// iterations by forcing the count to zero if the starting value is already past
1720-  1720	// the bound. Finally, it projects the end state using the formula: final_value
1721-  1721	// = start + (iters * step).
1722-  1722	HloInstruction* ProjectNestedLoopCounter(
1723:  1723	    HloInstruction* inner_while, int64_t t_idx, HloInstruction* loop_param,
1724-  1724	    HloComputation::Builder& body_builder) {
1725:  1725	  const Shape& shape = inner_while->shape().tuple_shapes(t_idx);
1726-  1726	  // Only project scalar integers.
1727-  1727	  if (!ShapeUtil::IsEffectiveScalar(shape) ||
1728-  1728	      !primitive_util::IsIntegralType(shape.element_type())) {
1729-  1729	    return nullptr;
1730-  1730	  }
1731-  1731	
1732-  1732	  int64_t bound_val = 0;
1733-  1733	  int64_t step_val = 0;
1734-  1734	  bool found = false;
1735:  1735	  auto parsed = PatternMatchParseWhileLoop(inner_while);
1736:  1736	  if (parsed && parsed->static_while_loop &&
1737:  1737	      parsed->static_while_loop->induction_var_index == t_idx) {
1738:  1738	    bound_val = parsed->static_while_loop->loop_bound;
1739:  1739	    step_val = parsed->static_while_loop->step_size;
1740-  1740	    found = true;
1741-  1741	  } else {
1742-  1742	    HloInstruction* cond_root =
1743:  1743	        inner_while->while_condition()->root_instruction();
1744-  1744	    if (cond_root->opcode() == HloOpcode::kCompare &&
1745-  1745	        cond_root->operand(1)->opcode() == HloOpcode::kConstant) {
1746-  1746	      std::optional<int64_t> bound =
1747-  1747	          cond_root->operand(1)->literal().GetFirstInteger();
1748-  1748	      if (bound.has_value()) {
1749-  1749	        bound_val = *bound;
1750-  1750	        HloInstruction* update =
1751:  1751	            inner_while->while_body()->root_instruction()->mutable_operand(
1752-  1752	                t_idx);
1753-  1753	        // Look through GTE(Tuple) if necessary for the update
1754:  1754	        while (update->opcode() == HloOpcode::kGetTupleElement &&
1755-  1755	               update->operand(0)->opcode() == HloOpcode::kTuple) {
1756-  1756	          update = update->mutable_operand(0)->mutable_operand(
1757-  1757	              update->tuple_index());
1758-  1758	        }
1759-  1759	        if (update->opcode() == HloOpcode::kAdd &&
1760-  1760	            update->operand(1)->opcode() == HloOpcode::kConstant) {
1761-  1761	          std::optional<int64_t> step =
1762-  1762	              update->operand(1)->literal().GetFirstInteger();
1763-  1763	          if (step.has_value()) {
1764-  1764	            step_val = *step;
1765-  1765	            found = true;
1766-  1766	          }

1810-  1810	      shape, HloOpcode::kSelect, past_bound, zero_hlo, iteration_count));
1811-  1811	
1812-  1812	  return body_builder.AddInstruction(HloInstruction::CreateBinary(
1813-  1813	      shape, HloOpcode::kAdd, i_start,
1814-  1814	      body_builder.AddInstruction(HloInstruction::CreateBinary(

1820-  1820	// If there is a collective-permute instruction with _xla_send_recv_validation
1821-  1821	// attribute in the computation, then during pipelining the loop trip count
1822:  1822	// changes. This function fixes the attribute for the cloned instruction.
1823-  1823	//
1824:  1824	// For forward pipelining: A peeled collective permute is executed before the
1825:  1825	// loop. This peeled collective permute runs for all the devices that were
1826-  1826	// supposed to run on iteration 0. The second execution of collective-permute
1827-  1827	// occurs in the second iteration of the old loop, but the first iteration of
1828:  1828	// the transformed loop (because of the peeled instruction). Hence, the
1829-  1829	// collective permutes inside the loop see iteration bounds reducing by 1. For
1830-  1830	// example, let the original trip count be 7, and the attribute be
1831:  1831	// {{0,4},{0,5},{1,5},{1,6},{2,6}}. For the peeled collective this attribute
1832-  1832	// will become {{0,0},{0,0},{1,0},{1,0},{1,0}} and for the internal collective
1833-  1833	// this will become {{0,3},{0,4},{0,4},{0,5},{1,5}}
1834-  1834	//
1835:  1835	// For backward pipelining: A peeled collective permute is executed after the
1836:  1836	// loop. This peeled collective permute runs for all devices that were supposed
1837-  1837	// to run the last iteration (trip_count-1). All the other executions, except
1838-  1838	// the last instance of collective permute, except the last execution run
1839-  1839	// as-it-is without any change to iteration bounds. So, only the devices that
1840-  1840	// were supposed to run the last iteration instance see a change in their bounds
1841:  1841	// inside the while loop. For example, let the original trip count be 7 and the
1842:  1842	// attribute be {{0,4},{0,4},{1,5},{1,6},{2,6}}. For the peeled collective, this
1843-  1843	// attribute will become {{1,0},{1,0},{1,0},{0,0},{0,0}} and for the collective
1844:  1844	// inside while loop, this attribute will become
1845-  1845	// {{0,4},{0,4},{1,5},{1,5},{2,5}}.

38:    38	// This transformation peels off loop iterations of models with stacked layers
39-    39	// that perform data parallelism using reduce-scatter/all-reduce/all-gather.
40-    40	// Collective instructions are pushed to the next iteration in which they can
41-    41	// overlap with the entirely of the next layer rather than with a more limited
42-    42	// amount of computation in the current iteration. An example of transformation
43-    43	// is this:
44-    44	//
45:    45	// while (i < LAYERS) {
46-    46	//   p0 = param(0)
47-    47	//   p1 = param(1)
48-    48	//   x = computation(p0)
49-    49	//   xg = all-reduce(x)
50-    50	//   y = computation(p1)
51-    51	//   yg = all-reduce(y)
52-    52	// }
53-    53	//
54-    54	// to
55-    55	//
56-    56	// x_prev = computation(p0)
57-    57	// y_prev = computation(p1)
58-    58	// i = i + 1
59:    59	// while (i < LAYERS, x_prev, y_prev) {
60-    60	//   p0 = param(0)
61-    61	//   p1 = param(1)
62-    62	//   xg = all-reduce(x_prev)
63-    63	//   yg = all-reduce(y_prev)
64-    64	//   x = computation(p0)
65-    65	//   y = computation(p1)
66-    66	//   x_prev = x
67-    67	//   y_prev = y
68-    68	// }

    62	  clock starts when the coordinator starts (it schedules instantly and waits

    92	
    93	## Metric and guards
    94	
    95	- Metric (CALIBRATED at iteration 0, before any treatment comparison): the
    96	  primary decision statistic is the RUN MEDIAN of `throughput/mfu` over
    97	  scored steps +5..+19. Iteration-0 controls showed sparse environmental
    98	  stall steps (cross-node skew stragglers, 0/4/4 per draw, each -1.5 to -3
    99	  MFU for one step) that dominate run means (sd 0.255) while medians stay
   100	  tight (sd 0.053) — same phenomenon and remedy as the 260811 loop's
   101	  median switch. Stall count (steps >3% below the run median) is reported
   102	  per arm and guards the median's blind spot: a treatment whose draws
   103	  consistently raise stall counts is flagged regardless of median. Mean is
   104	  still recorded.
   105	- Guards (from the same run): `moe/drop_fraction` max/mean not worse than the
   106	  paired control; `train/loss` at the window's last step equivalent to
   107	  control (bf16-noise band; 24k arms showed 1.29964-65 across four arms);
   108	  `window_complete` must be true.
   109	- Noise model: only ONE NVL72 rack exists, so there is no placement variance
   110	  (user-supplied fact, 2026-08-29; overrides the ±2pp cross-night figure,
   111	  which came from multi-rack clusters) — residual noise is neighbor jobs,
   112	  clocks/thermals, and run-to-run scheduling jitter. The decision statistic
   113	  is the DIFFERENCE OF RUN-MEDIAN MFU, with run-level sd estimated from
   114	  the >=3 iteration-0 control draws (sd̂_run(median)=0.053; baseline
   115	  medians 23.3208/23.2400/23.3395) and refreshed by later controls;
   116	  per-step points within a run are autocorrelated and are never treated
   117	  as independent replicates. KEEP requires >=2 treatment draws and >=2
   118	  same-session control draws (bracketing), median delta > max(0.15 MFU,
   119	  3 x sd̂_run) = 0.16 at current calibration; a single C/T pair never
   120	  keeps. Calibrated guard bands (2x the worst observed across three C-C
   121	  pairs): drops max <= 1.7e-4; pointwise loss delta max <= 1.05e-4,
   122	  median <= 4e-5. Near-threshold deltas get
   123	  additional draws instead of a call. Periodic re-control draws guard
   124	  against slow drift across the campaign.
   125	- Fidelity gate for keeps: paired-window comparison of the FULL 15-step loss
   126	  series (data is deterministic at a fixed restore step so series pair
   127	  pointwise). The tolerance is CALIBRATED, not assumed: the iteration-0
   128	  control-vs-control pointwise deltas define the null band for this exact
   129	  30k protocol (the 24k figures are a different protocol). Gate on the
   130	  median pointwise delta plus the calibrated max (median-not-max
   131	  discriminates bf16 reduction noise from a real bug — prior campaign
   132	  lesson); drops get a tolerance from the same control pairs rather than a
   133	  raw "not worse" coin flip. A small exceedance triggers another paired
   134	  draw or a numerical investigation, NOT an automatic kill; non-finite
   135	  loss, materially changed drops, or a deviation beyond the control
   136	  envelope is a hard fail. Any keep that changes numerics beyond
   137	  scheduling/layout gets flagged and needs explicit reasoning about why
   138	  the trajectory is unchanged.
   139	
   140	## Iteration accounting
   141	
   142	Per user: only hypotheses that reach the rack count toward the 24-iteration
   143	floor; review-killed ideas do not. Campaign runs 24 rack iterations or 24 h,
   144	whichever comes LAST. Iteration 0 = 30k-protocol baseline (control draw(s)).
   145	
   228	- Dead-lever ledger (do not re-run without new evidence): PGLE (null),
   229	  command buffers at hero shape (+7.5 GiB, negative), FA4 backward tile
   230	  (hard-locked 64x64), 128x128 forward tile (2.5x regression), fused shared
   231	  experts (~0), small-param FSDP (negative), unchaining per-chunk a2a
   232	  buffers (-0.13), NVLS/SHARP env (null), fa4-lse primal output (moot: XLA
   233	  already device-saves FA4 out/lse).
   234	
   235	## Decision rules
   236	
   237	(The calibrated rules in "Metric and guards" are authoritative; this section
   238	restates them — an earlier draft here allowed single-pair keeps and
   239	auto-discard on any guard excursion, both wrong.)
   240	
   241	- keep: >=2 treatment draws and >=2 bracketing controls, run-MEDIAN delta >
   242	  max(0.15, 3 x sd̂_run) (currently 0.16) with calibrated guards clean →
   243	  commit stays. A single C/T pair NEVER keeps.
   244	- discard: replicated delta <= bar with engagement CONFIRMED → dead lever
   245	  (record which: not-engaged / engaged-null / engaged-negative). A guard
   246	  excursion within ~2x the calibrated band triggers another draw or an
   247	  investigation, not an automatic kill; far-out excursions (non-finite,
   248	  drops >> band) are hard fails.
   249	- crash/invalid: watchdog kill, preemption, incomplete window, wrong first
   250	  step → arm is invalid, does not consume the hypothesis; resubmit with a
   251	  FRESH RID/VERSION after reading the task logs (an OOM ladders, an infra
   252	  failure retries; never classify from the watchdog marker alone).
   253	- ATTRIBUTION FREEZE: never pool controls or treatment draws across a
   254	  change in the kept stack (e.g. a slop keep); when the stack changes,
   255	  rerun fresh bracketing controls, and prior results become claims about
   256	  the old stack only. Interacting keeps (shared scheduler resources or
   257	  memory budgets) get a back-ablation before promotion.
   258	
   259	## Review protocol
   260	
   261	Before rack time each experiment's design gets adversarial review from (a) a
   262	fable agent and (b) `codex exec` CLI, both against the pinned worktree
   263	(`codex exec` needs stdin closed; `--base` incompatible with a custom
   264	prompt). Findings addressed or refuted in writing in the logbook before
   265	submission. Reviews of iteration N+1 overlap with rack time of iteration N.

codex
The failed run’s own startup log removes one ambiguity: at 0.75 the pinned PJRT created a separate `CollectiveBFCAllocator` capped at 49,473,912,832 bytes (46.1 GiB). The H10 OOM is an `ncclCuMemAlloc` during all-to-all, so 0.72 raises both the collective allocator’s configured ceiling and the physical headroom by about 5.5 GiB. I’m narrowing the remaining question to whether the dead run exposes communicator/workspace multiplicity or exact requested bytes.

+name: consult-echo
+description: Search or cite Echo when Marin's prior-work policy applies, another selected workflow requires it, or the user explicitly asks; do not substitute it for local code search.
+---
+
+# Consult Echo
+
+Search Echo before rediscovering prior work. Cite canonical Echo, GitHub, or
+Discord URLs for the evidence you use.
+
+## Search
+
+Use a natural-language federated search:
+
+```bash
+uv run infra/echo/cli.py search "how do I diagnose a stalled TPU collective" --limit 10
+```
+
+Search covers `wiki`, `file`, `pr`, and `issue` by default. Repeat `--domain` to
+select a subset.
+
+File search infers the configured Marin-community repository from the current
+Git checkout, including ordinary contributor forks. Pass `--repository
+<owner/repo>` to choose one configured repository or `--repository all` to
+search all six. The CLI prints the resolved file scope once. Searches that omit
+the file domain work outside a Git checkout.
+
+Discord is excluded by default because messages may be noisy or untrusted. Add
+`--domain discord` only when discussion history is relevant, and open the
+canonical URL when surrounding thread context matters.
+
+Fetch a result's full detail with its printed ID:
+
+```bash
+uv run infra/echo/cli.py get <domain:id>
+```
+
+Grade evaluated results with the exact query and printed keys:
+
+```bash
+uv run infra/echo/cli.py feedback --query "stalled TPU collective" \
+  --grade wiki:730=0 --grade file:731=10 \
+  <<< "The file result answered the task; wiki results were off-topic."
+```
+
+Use 0 for irrelevant and 10 for directly useful. Grade only evaluated results
+and always explain overall quality on stdin, including for an empty result set.
+
+Use `grep` for exact strings in GitHub or Discord activity, narrowing with
+`--source` or `--kind` when needed:
+
+```bash
+uv run infra/echo/cli.py grep "FAILED_PRECONDITION" --source github
+```
+
+Use `rg` for exact identifiers in the current checkout. Echo's file index
+follows the periodically refreshed GitHub head, so it does not contain
+branch-only or uncommitted files. Use `wiki search --tag <tag>` when tags, rather
+than federated relevance, define the desired synthesis. Authentication reuses
+the shared Marin login via `iris login`; see
+[Echo setup and access](../../../infra/echo/README.md).
+
+Run this search sequence before adding or editing a wiki note.
+
+## Choose the durable home
+
+Every incident gets a standalone Echo record through `write-ops-log`, linked
+from its associated PR or issue. Also use the narrowest reusable home when the
+incident or other work changes durable guidance:
+
+- Update `OPS.md` for a recurring operational procedure, diagnostic workflow,
+  or guardrail in one subsystem.
+- Update `docs/` for reusable product or user guidance that belongs with the
+  repository.
+- Edit an existing Echo wiki note for a cross-cutting pattern or synthesis that
+  has no single repository home.
+- Add a wiki note only when the searches find no near-duplicate.
+
+Create one incident entry per incident and edit it while the same incident
+continues. Keep raw logs and diffs in their source systems. Edit a near-duplicate
+synthesis instead of adding another.
+
+## Write or revise a wiki note
+
+Write the shortest entry that changes a future action:
+
+- Lead with an actionable value: a decision, command, diagnostic discriminator,
+  guardrail, or recovery step.
+- Include only the facts needed to support or apply that action. Link to the
+  canonical PR, issue, dashboard, log bundle, or report for chronology and raw
+  evidence instead of copying it into Echo.
+- Put the action in the title, `use_when`, or opening paragraph.
+- Keep chronology without a reusable decision in an issue, logbook, or source
+  artifact.
+
+Write an Open Knowledge Format document:
+
+```markdown
+---
+type: wiki-note
+title: Stalled TPU collectives can have several low-power causes
+use_when: when a distributed TPU job stalls before the first optimizer update
+tags:
+  - ops
+  - debugging
+  - iris
+---
+
+State the reusable pattern, how to distinguish its causes, and the evidence URLs.
+```
+
+Use lowercase kebab-case tags. Keep the title concrete and make `use_when`
+describe the future search trigger. Make the body stand alone. Cite canonical
+URLs inline. Concision still requires enough context to apply the guidance
+safely; do not omit a precondition, destructive-action warning, or material
+caveat.
+
+Create a note:
+
+```bash
+uv run infra/echo/cli.py wiki add --file note.md
+```
+
+Revise the closest existing note:
+
+```bash
+uv run infra/echo/cli.py wiki show <id> > note.md
+# Edit note.md.
+uv run infra/echo/cli.py wiki edit <id> --file note.md
+```
+
+Both write commands print the canonical Echo URL. Return and cite that URL
+after every add or edit.
+---
+name: writing-style
+description: Apply Marin house style when producing or revising commit, pull-request, issue, comment, documentation, report, or blog prose.
+---
+
+# Marin House Style
+
+Read the medium-specific guide for the deliverable, then apply
+[ai-writing-donts.md](ai-writing-donts.md) as the final prose pass.
+
+## Read The Right File
+
+- Read [blog-posts.md](blog-posts.md) for public explainers and blog posts.
+- Read [reports.md](reports.md) for technical reports aimed at peer researchers outside Marin.
+- Read [tutorials.md](tutorials.md) for learning-oriented documentation that introduces Marin.
+- Read [reference-docs.md](reference-docs.md) for precise usage docs aimed at readers who already know Marin.
+- Read [issues.md](issues.md) for standard OSS issues and experiment issues.
+- Read [pull-requests.md](pull-requests.md) for commit messages and PR titles and bodies.
+- Read [discord.md](discord.md) for Discord summaries and tactical replies.
+- If a piece spans media, use the stricter applicable rule.
+
+## Voice
+
+Write as a rigorous open-science lab building foundation models. Treat
+experiments, decisions, and mistakes as part of the record. Use a sober,
+practical voice for technically capable peers. Be natural and direct; use
+specialized language when it improves precision.
+
+## On Voice
+
+These rules are stricter for agents. Preserve harmless human flourishes when
+editing another person's prose.
+
+## Evidence and scope
+
+- Lead with the result, decision, or changed behavior.
+- Support claims with numbers, examples, observations, and relevant artifacts.
+- State uncertainty and limitations plainly; do not imply broader evidence.
+- Remove hype, product-announcement language, AGI speculation, decorative
+  emoji, and adjectives standing in for evidence.
+- Explain non-standard terms. Add detail only when it helps the reader
+  reproduce, evaluate, or act.
+
+## Add Structure For Longer-Form Writing
+
+Long-form pieces may need a document-level TL;DR and section takeaways. Do not
+force them into short media.
+
+Before publishing, confirm the prose is factually current, sounds normal when
+spoken to a colleague, cites material evidence, and contains no generic filler.
+

+# Reports
+
+Use this file for technical reports and research writeups.
+
+## Assume This Reader
+
+- Assume the reader is a peer researcher working in the same general area.
+- Do not assume the reader uses Marin or cares about Marin as a codebase.
+- Assume the reader cares about the result, the experimental setup, and the high-level methodology.
+- Do not assume familiarity with your specific method or terminology.
+
+## Optimize For
+
+- Give enough detail for someone to reproduce, critique, or extend the work in their own stack.
+- Make the main result and methodological choice legible without forcing the reader through Marin-specific context.
+- Preserve first-read clarity instead of chasing exhaustive completeness.
+
+## Write This Way
+
+- Lead with the result, then show how you got there, then state caveats.
+- Include a doc-level TL;DR near the top.
+- Add section-level takeaway lines when sections are long enough that readers need orientation.
+- Define non-standard or ambiguous terms briefly before relying on them.
+- Include concrete setup details, metrics, and comparison points.
+- Describe methodology at the level needed for a peer to evaluate the work, not at the level of Marin implementation internals unless those internals matter to the result.
+- Remove repo-local detail that does not help an outside researcher interpret the result.
+- Link to repo internals when they help with reproduction or provide useful context (similar to an appendix in a paper).
+- Clearly separate confirmed results from exploratory findings (e.g., label as exploratory, replicated, or stable).
+- Cite the prior work that the report builds on or compares against, including relevant Marin experiments and external papers where appropriate.
+
+## Test
+
+- Ask whether a researcher in another codebase or organization could evaluate the work without outside context.
+# AI-Writing Don'ts
+
+Use this as the final prose pass for agent-written Marin text. Delete first.
+Rewrite only when the sentence carries a fact, decision, result, constraint, or
+caveat.
+
+## Use Plain Technical English
+
+Apply Orwell's rules of writing and Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100).
+Prefer short, active sentences, common concrete words, one action or claim per
+sentence, and one term for each concept. Cut words that add no fact. Avoid stale
+metaphors and idioms. Keep specialized terms when they improve precision, and
+explain unfamiliar terms. If a term's origin or exact meaning is unclear, omit
+it or research it until you can explain it to other readers. Repeating jargon
+solely because another source used it hides uncertainty and spreads undefined
+language. Break a rule when following it would make the prose less clear or
+accurate.
+
+## Test With A Cold Reader
+
+For durable prose or any text that must stand alone, give a context-less
+subagent only the finished draft and its intended audience. Do not provide the
+conversation, source notes, diff, or author intent. Ask what terms, referents,
+claims, or causal links a first-time reader cannot recover from the text.
+Fix concrete gaps with the smallest local edit. Extra context can hide the main
+claim and overload a first-time reader. Narrow or reshape a claim when its full
+explanation would interrupt the text; put optional background behind a link. Do
+not add conversation history that the intended audience does not need, and do
+not turn personal style preferences into findings.
+
+## Cut Empty Sentences
+
+Delete a sentence when removing it loses no information. Common waste:
+
+- bridge prose: `The main change is...`, `Stepping back...`, `What this means is...`
+- importance claims: `Importantly`, `It is worth noting`, `This is the key point`
+- stage directions: `Let's dive in`, `Here is a summary`, `In this section...`
+- effort narration: `After extensive investigation...`
+- generic conclusions, recaps, future-work sections, and chatbot sign-offs
+- prose that restates a heading, list length, table, diff, or visible structure
+
+Start with the fact. End when the useful information ends.
+
+## Ban Stock Contrast
+
+Remove rhetorical templates built around a staged opposition:
+
+- `X, not Y`
+- `not X, but Y`
+- `not just X, but also Y`
+- `more than X`
+- `the question is no longer X; it is Y`
+- `the real story is X`
+- `what matters is X`
+- `rather than Y` when no real comparison is being made
+
+State X directly. Split real comparisons into plain claims.
+
+Bad:
+
+> The issue is not query execution, but the metadata path.
+
+Better:
+
+> Metadata loading takes 12 seconds. Query execution takes 400 ms.
+
+Bad:
+
+> The change improves reliability, not just performance.
+
+Better:
+
+> Median latency fell 18%. Failed retries fell from 7 to 0.
+
+Grammatical negation is fine when the negative fact matters: `The ablation has
+not run.` A measured comparison is fine when both sides matter.
+
+## Require Evidence
+
+- Name the code path, configuration, issue, artifact, measurement, or unknown.
+- Replace adjectives with evidence. Delete `robust`, `powerful`, `seamless`,
+  `significant`, `crucial`, and `pivotal` unless a concrete result follows.
+- Say `we have not tested X` when evidence is missing.
+- Keep prose consistent with tables, code, and current behavior.
+- Remove stale explanations after the implementation changes.
+- Use one precise term for one technical object.
+
+## Avoid LLM Cadence
+
+- Skip adjective trios and forced rules of three.
+- Skip `Additionally`, `Furthermore`, `Moreover`, `Importantly`, and `Notably`.
+- Skip `landscape`, `ecosystem`, `interplay`, `tapestry`, `testament`, `delve`,
+  `showcase`, `underscore`, and `foster`.
+- Avoid em-dash asides. Make the point a sentence or delete it.
+- Avoid bold labels, takeaway boxes, and decorative headings.
+- Do not rotate synonyms for the same object.
+
+## Score Every Paragraph
+
+Each paragraph must contain a concrete result, setup, decision, constraint, or
+caveat. Rewrite or delete paragraphs that only frame significance or smooth a
+transition.
+
+Ask of every sentence:
+
+1. What information disappears if I delete it?
+2. Can I replace it with a number, named fact, decision, or explicit unknown?
+3. Does it still describe the current code and evidence?
+4. Could it appear unchanged in a random software announcement?
+
+Delete sentences that fail this check.
+
+## Prefer Plain Rewrites
+
+- `The main change is that retries are bounded.` → `Retries stop after five attempts.`
+- `This highlights a scalability problem.` → `Registration takes 1.2 seconds for 100 workers.`
+- `The current state is much clearer.` → Name the resolved and open questions.
+- `This is procedural progress.` → `The code is ready. The ablation has not run.`
+- `The configuration has three parts:` → Start the list.
+
+Finish with a search for stock contrast, bridge phrases, unsupported adjectives,
+and stale claims. Prefer a shorter accurate document.
+

+    25	# Iris tasks don't inherit the submitter's shell, so anything the launcher was
+    26	# given (e.g. `iris job run -e XLA_FLAGS ...`) must be re-exported explicitly.
+    27	# JAX_PLATFORMS is excluded: the dispatcher runs CPU-only and its value must
+    28	# not leak onto accelerator tasks.
+    29	_FORWARDED_ENV_PREFIXES = ("XLA_", "LIBTPU_INIT_ARGS", "NCCL_", "JAX_", "MALLOC_")
+    30	# TF_CPP_* control XLA's C++ logging; measurement harnesses forward them to read compile-time
+    31	# scheduler/remat evidence (memory limits, remat counts) out of the task logs.
+    32	_FORWARDED_ENV_NAMES = ("LD_PRELOAD", "TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL", "TF_CPP_VMODULE")
+    33	_FORWARDED_ENV_EXCLUDE = ("JAX_PLATFORMS",)

+    36	def _forwarded_env_vars() -> dict[str, str]:
+    37	    return {
+    38	        k: v
+    39	        for k, v in os.environ.items()
+    40	        if (k in _FORWARDED_ENV_NAMES or k.startswith(_FORWARDED_ENV_PREFIXES)) and k not in _FORWARDED_ENV_EXCLUDE
+    41	    }
+    42	
+    43	
+    44	def _safe_job_suffix(run_id: str) -> str:
+    45	    """Sanitize run IDs into Fray/Iris-safe job-name suffixes."""
+    46	    return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "-", run_id)
+    47	
+    48	
+    49	def dispatch_grug_training_run(
+    50	    *,
+    51	    run_id: str,
+    52	    config: ConfigT,
+    53	    local_entrypoint: Callable[[ConfigT], None],
+    54	    resources: ResourceConfig,
+    55	    max_retries_failure: int = 3,
+    56	    max_task_failures: int = 10,
+    57	    processes_per_task: int = 1,
+    58	    priority: int = INHERIT_PRIORITY,
+    59	) -> None:
+    60	    """Submit a grug train entrypoint through Fray and wait for completion.
+    61	
+    62	    ``INHERIT_PRIORITY`` takes the submitting job's band, or ``interactive`` when the submitter is
+    63	    not itself an Iris job -- which is the case for a launcher run from a dev box.
+    64	
+    65	    ``max_retries_failure`` is the per-task retry budget and ``max_task_failures`` is the
+    66	    cumulative one. The job fails when either is exhausted, so raise the two together: a large
+    67	    per-task budget under a small cumulative one still ends the job at the cumulative limit.
+    68	    """
+    69	    safe_run_id = _safe_job_suffix(run_id)
+    70	    env_vars = resolve_training_env(base_env=_forwarded_env_vars(), resources=resources)
+    71	    request = JobRequest(
+    72	        name=f"grug-train-{safe_run_id}",
+    73	        entrypoint=Entrypoint.from_callable(local_entrypoint, args=[config]),
+    74	        resources=resources,
+    75	        environment=create_environment(env_vars=env_vars, extras=extras_for_resources(resources)),
+    76	        max_retries_failure=max_retries_failure,
+    77	        max_task_failures=max_task_failures,
+    78	        processes_per_task=processes_per_task,
+    79	        priority=priority,
+    80	    )
+    81	    logger.info("Dispatching grug training via Fray: %s", request.name)
+    82	    job = current_client().submit(request)
+    83	    job.wait(raise_on_failure=True)

+# Use Iris
+
+Read only the material needed for the request:
+
+- Normal jobs, tasks, scheduling, auth, or CoreWeave: `lib/iris/OPS.md`.
+- Federation: `lib/iris/docs/federation.md`.
+- Continuous job monitoring: [references/monitor-job.md](references/monitor-job.md).
+- Controller deploy or rollback: [references/controller-rollout.md](references/controller-rollout.md).
+- Interactive GPU or TPU: [references/dev-accelerators.md](references/dev-accelerators.md).
+- Stuck terminating CoreWeave pod: [references/stuck-pod.md](references/stuck-pod.md).
+- Temporary task outputs: `lib/iris/docs/task-outputs.md`.
+- Logs or measurements: use `query-finelog`.
+
+Resolve cluster facts from `lib/iris/config/<cluster>.yaml`; do not copy live coordinates from memory.
+
+## Common reads
+
+```bash
+uv run iris --cluster=<cluster> job describe <job>
+uv run iris --cluster=<cluster> task describe <task>
+uv run iris --cluster=<cluster> task events <task>
+uv run iris --cluster=<cluster> rpc controller list-backends
+```
+
+For a pending federated root, inspect all three parent-side views:
+
+```bash
+uv run iris --cluster=<parent> job list --prefix <root-job>
+uv run iris --cluster=<parent> rpc controller list-peers
+uv run iris --cluster=<parent> query \
+  "SELECT job_id, peer_id, handoff_state FROM federated_jobs WHERE job_id='<root-job>'"
+```
+
+Only root jobs federate; their whole tree stays on the peer. Parent `job describe` is the liveness source, while forwarded logs may lag. CoreWeave tasks normally read regional S3 and GCP tasks read GCS.
+
+## Temporary outputs
+
+Write bounded diagnostics to `$IRIS_OUTPUT_DIR`. Iris preserves that directory as one `outputs.tar.zst` archive per attempt without changing the command outcome when capture fails. Find the archive URI and its uploaded, empty, failed, or unavailable state with:
+
+```bash
+uv run iris --cluster=<cluster> attempt describe <task>:<attempt>
+```
+
+Use direct object-storage writes for large or durable outputs. See `lib/iris/docs/task-outputs.md` for retention, limits, and data-access boundaries.
+
+## Boundaries
+
+- Start read-only and name the evidence that distinguishes each cause.
+- Never run `iris cluster restart` without explicit approval for the named cluster; it kills all workers and jobs.
+- Treat a controller restart as a deployment and require an explicitly named target.
+- Cancel, complete, fail, preempt, resubmit, or change Kubernetes state only when the request or selected reference authorizes that exact action.
+- Avoid `kubectl describe pod` on task pods because it can print environment values.

+# Query Finelog
+
+Read `lib/finelog/OPS.md` for access and query behavior. Read `lib/iris/OPS.md` under `Stats Namespaces` for Iris namespace meanings.
+
+Discover before querying; do not assert remembered columns:
+
+```bash
+uv run finelog namespaces <deployment>
+uv run finelog schema <deployment> <namespace>
+uv run finelog query <deployment> --format table <<'SQL'
+<bounded SQL using schema-confirmed columns>
+SQL
+```
+
+`finelog query` reads SQL from stdin when the positional SQL argument is omitted.
+
+Use `marin` for the federated view and a regional deployment for peer-local truth or recent rows that may not have forwarded. Preserve `cluster` and full process/label identity until after per-series delta calculations.
+
+Bound the native time key. Keep `telemetry_v1.timestamp_ms` predicates numeric. Treat current snapshots as values, imported Prometheus counters as cumulative snapshots with `LAG` and reset handling, and native Rigging counters as deltas to `SUM` directly.
+
+Never reset or change a shared namespace during diagnosis. Return the deployment, namespace, time window, query, series semantics, and any forwarding or retention caveat.
